Fonts

WordPress 6.5 added a Font Library (Appearance → Fonts) to upload font files or install Google Fonts and make them available to the Site Editor’s typography settings.

What WordPress does here
The Font Library lists the fonts the active theme provides, lets you upload .woff2/.ttf files, and installs fonts from Google Fonts. Chosen fonts become options in Styles → Typography.
What Drupal does instead
Drupal core has no font library. Fonts are part of the theme: Umami ships Scope One and Open Sans in its CSS; Olivero uses Lora and Metropolis. Changing fonts means editing the theme (or a sub-theme) or installing a contrib module.

Permalink Settings

WordPress offers permalink structures such as /%year%/%monthnum%/%postname%/ and lets you set a category and tag base. Drupal gives every piece of content a system path (/node/12) and an optional URL alias, with no built-in pattern.

What WordPress does here
Common Settings: Plain, Day and name, Month and name, Numeric, Post name, Custom Structure. Optional: Category base and Tag base.

Privacy

As a website owner, you may need to follow national or international privacy laws. For example, you may need to create and display a privacy policy. WordPress keeps a designated Privacy Policy page and links it from the login screen; Drupal core has no such designation, so this setting is stored by the WordPress-style admin module and the page is an ordinary Basic page. Linking it in the footer is done in Menus.
